The mean can hide a wide spread

Predict: can a sample with a mean of1% still contain both negative and positive months?

Original hypothetical teaching example. This complete static route needs no JavaScript or animation. The interactive walkthrough is available inside the chapter.

On a narrow screen, scroll the diagram horizontally. Every value and step is also explained below.

Step 4/4: Use the sample denominator
Sample SD=√(58/(6−1))≈3.406 percentage points. Dividing by n−1 is the sample convention. Neither mean nor SD is a future guarantee.

All steps and numerical explanations

  1. Keep every observation

    Six invented monthly returns:−3,−1,0,1,2,7 percent. Each bar is one observation, not a future probability.

  2. Locate the mean

    The sum is6%; divide by six observations to get mean 1%.

  3. Keep the deviations

    Deviations from 1% are−4,−2,−1,0,1,6 percentage points. The squared deviations sum to 58.

  4. Use the sample denominator

    Sample SD=√(58/(6−1))≈3.406 percentage points. Dividing by n−1 is the sample convention. Neither mean nor SD is a future guarantee.

Six synthetic observations; descriptive statistics only. Annual scaling and probability forecasts need additional assumptions.
